CRDs, controllers, operators, scheduler extensions and CSI allow the platform to be adapted without changing the entire core.
The same declarative state model applies across workloads, networking, storage, configuration and infrastructure.

aliasGroups.label: C
aliasGroups.rationale: Reviewed records identify the C programming language. Language influence, host syntax and implementation-language assertions remain distinct edges, not identity proof for C++.

aliasGroups.label: C++
aliasGroups.rationale: All variants explicitly label the C++ language; CUDA C/C++ extension and C with Classes remain separate.

aliasGroups.label: Ruby
aliasGroups.rationale: Named Ruby language, not Rails framework or a specific Ruby implementation/runtime.

aliasGroups.label: Python
aliasGroups.rationale: Named Python language; source claims about its reference implementation do not turn the language into CPython.

aliasGroups.label: GCC
aliasGroups.rationale: Same named compiler collection, C/C++ frontend roles preserved in variants.

aliasGroups.label: Clang
aliasGroups.rationale: Same named compiler frontend with distinct C and CUDA compilation assertions.

aliasGroups.label: LLVM
aliasGroups.rationale: Named compiler infrastructure, not Clang or nvcc.

aliasGroups.label: Unix
aliasGroups.rationale: Named Unix OS family; source implementation/history assertions preserved.

aliasGroups.label: CPU
aliasGroups.rationale: Generic CPU processor class, not host role, GPU or instruction set.

aliasGroups.label: Operating system
aliasGroups.rationale: OS definition identifies the general software concept; optical mount_interface integrates_with the same general operating system and exposes filesystem data. Not an OS-specific implementation.

aliasGroups.label: Linux
aliasGroups.rationale: All four records explicitly type Linux as an OS/platform. Source edges describe Docker support, OS services, optical media and ext4 use. Linux application sandboxing and Linux kernel remain separate.

aliasGroups.label: Microsoft Windows
aliasGroups.rationale: Windows/Microsoft Windows OS records: Docker platform, OS services/NTFS, optical version family and volume management. Named Windows versions and sandbox implementations are not merged.

aliasGroups.label: Go
aliasGroups.rationale: Both Python records identify the named programming language: Grumpy targets Go and Python influenced Go; Kubernetes identifies Go as its implementation language. Influence is a relationship, not a separate language identity.

aliasGroups.label: .NET Common Language Runtime
aliasGroups.rationale: Sandbox names .NET Common Language Runtime and its CAS/security role; VM source names the same managed process runtime. Roles remain in original variants.

aliasGroups.label: Sandbox
aliasGroups.rationale: OS relationships[313] provides foundational isolation mechanisms; sandbox definition identifies the security mechanism. VM software-sandbox use case remains scoped.

aliasGroups.label: Java Virtual Machine
aliasGroups.rationale: Python relationships[310] runs Jython on Java VM; VM relationships[33] explicitly classifies Java Virtual Machine as a process VM. Python VM is excluded.

aliasGroups.label: Kubernetes
aliasGroups.rationale: All three source definitions identify the Kubernetes platform; K8s is its abbreviation.

aliasGroups.label: Virtual Machine
aliasGroups.rationale: The Docker abbreviation and both full-name records refer to the VM concept, not to a particular VM instance.

aliasGroups.label: Linux Namespaces
aliasGroups.rationale: Both records describe the Linux kernel isolation mechanism; Kubernetes resource namespaces are excluded.

aliasGroups.label: Linux cgroups
aliasGroups.rationale: Both records describe the Linux kernel control-group mechanism.

aliasGroups.label: Application Dependency
aliasGroups.rationale: Singular/plural records describe software dependencies bundled with an application; the library subtype remains separate.

aliasGroups.label: OpenShift
aliasGroups.rationale: Spelling variants identify the same named OpenShift platform in both source definitions.

aliasGroups.label: FreeBSD jail
aliasGroups.rationale: Singular/plural records identify the same named FreeBSD jail technology.

aliasGroups.label: Application Portability
aliasGroups.rationale: Definitions all describe moving packaged applications between execution environments; infrastructure/API portability remains distinct.

operating_system:vm.label: Virtual machine (OS taxonomy)
operating_system:vm.rationale: OS relationships[317] connects virtual_machine to vm as same_concept_family; they are not merged.

python_language:vm.label: Python virtual machine
python_language:vm.rationale: Python relationships[193-194] identifies CPython bytecode runtime, not a generic system VM.

sandbox_computer_security:linux.label: Linux application sandboxing
sandbox_computer_security:linux.rationale: Sandbox relationships[25-27] identifies an implementation built on seccomp/cgroups/namespaces, not the Linux OS.

python_language:namespace.label: Python Namespace
python_language:namespace.rationale: Python runtime name binding is not Kubernetes resource grouping.

sandbox_computer_security:isolation.label: Sandbox Isolation
sandbox_computer_security:isolation.rationale: Sandbox security property is broader than VM-environment separation.

virtual_machine:isolation.label: VM Isolation
virtual_machine:isolation.rationale: VM environment separation remains distinct from generic sandbox security property.

sandbox_computer_security:ios.label: iOS/iPadOS sandboxing
sandbox_computer_security:ios.rationale: Source implementation record is the application sandbox, not the OS product.

docker:host.label: Docker Host
docker:host.rationale: Docker host can be a physical machine or VM; the VM document explicitly defines host as a physical machine.

virtual_machine:host.label: VM Host
virtual_machine:host.rationale: Physical host role retained separately from the broader Docker host role.

kubernetes:namespace.label: Kubernetes Namespace
kubernetes:namespace.rationale: Kubernetes resource grouping is not Linux kernel isolation.

declinedMerges.rationale: OS same_concept_family edge[317] must survive; Python bytecode runtime relationships[193-194] are not system-VM identities.
Linux application sandboxing implementation, Linux OS and Linux kernel have distinct scopes.
Security mechanism and software-sandbox use-case record remain distinct.
Generic logical storage, Docker persistence and Kubernetes mounted storage are not synonyms.
Optical filesystem remains distinct from generic filesystem; no speculative identity is introduced.
System-image relationship[3] is conditional on all relevant state being on disk, not an identity; optical relationship[0] is classification.
Docker image is a product-specific artifact; the other record is OCI-oriented and generic. Keep the narrower/broader distinction and add a typed editorial edge.
The source distinguishes orchestration technology from a cooperating-daemon cluster and a cluster grouping. Do not erase that distinction based on the shared Docker Swarm label.
The generic source record does not explicitly identify AIX; insufficient evidence for an identity merge.
Generic Virtuozzo versus specifically branded Parallels Virtuozzo Containers may carry product/version scope; retain both.
Docker service is an orchestration abstraction; Kubernetes Service is a network abstraction.
Product-specific storage objects have different scopes and lifecycles.
Linux kernel process isolation and Kubernetes API resource grouping are different concepts.
Identical labels hide different physical/virtual host scopes; split the previous automatic merge.
Container, Kubernetes, and general computer-cluster scopes are not identical.
General kernel, Linux implementation, shared-kernel model, and sharing mechanism are not identities.
Application portability, infrastructure/API portability, and process-VM platform independence are different scopes.
Keep generic activities separate from Kubernetes-specific mechanisms or example workloads.
Runtime unit, image artifact, Pod grouping, VM abstraction/subtypes, runtime category and implementations are not synonyms.

audit.policy: No fuzzy identities. Original records and all parallel source edges retained. Editorial edges do not repair or endorse source claims.
